fixes.done: Adopted, with two changes I can justify. Spec 6.4: when the 1 s and 2 s resends run out, the call now goes to a new freshRejected(acct). It throws hold.reason if a hold is active. Otherwise it adds one to freshRejects; on the third (maxSameRefreshError) it calls clearIf (sign-in-ended); before that it calls failed(), so the doubling hold blocks refreshes. A 401 on a token under transientHoldMs (30 s) old never starts a refresh and never clears at once (the critic's third fix). The rotated-meanwhile check now runs before that check, once per call, so a token killed by a rotation is still retried with the current one. First change: the count is a separate freshRejects, not sameError. Every refused token comes from a refresh that succeeded, and a success resets sameError, so sameError could never reach 3. freshRejects is reset only by a non-401 authenticated answer, a sign-in commit or a sign-out; failed() and the limit are reused. Second change: the 30 s window keys on obtainedAt for every token, sign-in tokens included, because the account does not record where a token came from and the same propagation risk applies. Also updated: L-12, L-14, the 2.1 table (new row), 6.3 step 2 and 6.7 step 3 (they reset freshRejects), 6.5 'When refreshes happen' and 'Clearing the hold', known limit 15 (now about 70 s or more before the clear), DR-4 (decision, alternative (h) with its reason, trade-off), F-8, T-4, DO-16 and the BREAKDOWN U5 row (pre-mortem 9). Tests: refresh test 10 gains the refused-token case (at most 3 refreshes, renewalHeld true between them, then sign-in-ended) and the slow-token case (exactly one refresh). The test file's default token age is now over transientHoldMs. The C-6 case says only a clock step reaches it. One knock-on: e2e journey B step 6, T-9 and the U8 row now wait 30 s, not 5 s (budget about 2 minutes), and the U7 journey forces its 401 on a token older than transientHoldMs. Guard row added.

Adopted in part, and the docs say why. TokenResult 'unusable' now carries its status. In renew, an unusable answer counts through sameOrFail('status:'+s, from, g0), the same helper the unknown codes use; sameError is now {key, count}, and the reset rule became 'not error and not unusable'. The same status three times in a row clears the account as sign-in-ended: that covers a 4xx whose parseable body has no error (GitHub's JSON message form) and a 2xx without access_token. Changed from the fix: a 3xx only holds, because at the token endpoint it is the signature of a captive portal or proxy (the case the critic called too aggressive to clear). The critic's 'HTML page' example is wrong under the spec: classifier row 4 makes an HTML body transient, not unusable, so it stays hold-only. Updated: departure 3, L-12, the 3.5 TokenResult and 5.3 rows 2 and 8, 6.5 (code and a 'Why unusable counts' bullet), DR-4 (decision, alternative (i) with its reason), F-7, T-4, DO-1 (a 3xx or unparseable failure only holds, so record it), UD-6 'Why', the spec's Day-one DO-1 line and the U1 row. Tests: new refresh test 4b (a 401 with a JSON message body three times clears after at most 3 requests, a 2xx without a token likewise, a 302 or a 400 HTML page only holds); the oauth shape test pins the status; refresh test 7 says three in a row clear. Guard row added.

Adopted the critic's first option. The rollback now runs inside replace, under the same lock. The public rollback() is gone. replace takes a kind, 'sign-in' or 'refresh', which also carries GS-10. On a failed commit, a sign-in either returns null (its admit fails: a sign-out began) or rewrites the file to the previous account and throws ReplaceFailure(false). If that rewrite also fails, it follows the file through steps 6 and 7 and returns the new account. A refresh's failed commit still throws ReplaceFailure(true). Updated: 3.6 (API and the ReplaceFailure comment), 4.3 step 5 (the separate rollback paragraph removed), the 4.5 crash row, 6.3 step 1 (rewritten for the three results), store tests (failure kinds, rollback, plus the critic's queued-writer test: file and live agree, and reopen plus reconcile gives the refreshed account with no orphans), device test 15, the guard row, DR-2 (decision, new alternative (e) with the race), F-10, T-3, the BREAKDOWN U2 listing, row and pre-mortem 6, the U5 row, and the traceability row (F-10 now maps to U2 as well).

findings.problem: REQUIREMENTS T-4 still says "a second 401 (account cleared)" with no age condition. Under GS-1, a second 401 on the just-refreshed or just-rotated token, which is always under 30 s old in real timing, holds and counts instead of clearing. Only a retry on a token at least transientHoldMs old clears the account. A builder writing tests from T-4 would therefore assert the behaviour GS-1 removed.
findings.evidence: REQUIREMENTS.md:145 (T-4): "401, refresh, retry; a 401 after a rotation (retry with the current token, no refresh); a second 401 (account cleared)". Spec refresh test 10 (l.1256): "A retry with a rotated token at least transientHoldMs old that still gets 401 clears the account."

findings.problem: The signed-in dialog's renewalHeld sentence no longer matches the hold behaviour after GS-4 and GS-1. It says reads wait while renewal is held. After GS-4, a read whose access token is still valid is sent during a hold and succeeds. During a GS-1 hold, reads are sent with the refused token and fail. Only reads that need a refresh fail without a request.
findings.evidence: Spec 8.2 l.968: "If renewalHeld: 'MoonAliza could not renew your GitHub sign-in just now, so GitHub reads wait until it can. If this continues, sign in again.'" Spec 6.4 usable() step 5 (l.711, GS-4). REQUIREMENTS F-6 (GS-4): "a call whose access token is still valid, even inside the 300 s margin, is sent with it". DR-4 trade-off "Reads during a hold" (DECISIONS.md:199).
findings.fix: Reword the sentence, for example: "MoonAliza could not renew your GitHub sign-in just now, so some GitHub reads fail until it can. If this continues, sign in again." The panel test only checks that the text renders, so no test changes.

checked: GS-1: resolved. I traced spec 6.4 send()/freshRejected and 6.5 renew in three cases. (1) Every refresh is accepted and every resource read gets 401, with reads 6 s apart: refresh 1, then a reject that sets a 30 s hold; reads during the hold throw hold.reason without counting; refresh 2 and refresh 3 follow, and the third reject clears as sign-in-ended. That is 3 refresh requests and about 70 s, matching known limit 15 and DR-4. (2) GitHub answers 401 until 8 s after a token is issued: exactly one refresh, the next read succeeds, and freshRejects goes back to 0. (3) C-6 is reached only by a clock step past transientHoldMs. freshRejects is reset in 6.3 step 2, in 6.7 step 3 and on any answer other than 401, and a successful refresh keeps it. These agree across L-12, L-14, the 2.1 row, 6.5 'When refreshes happen' and 'Clearing the hold', DR-4 (h), F-8, T-4 (except RF-2), DO-16, U5 pre-mortem 9, T-9, the U7 and U8 journeys and the guard row.

GS-2: resolved. TokenResult 'unusable' carries its status. sameOrFail keys on 'status:'+s, and error codes match ^[a-z_]{1,64}$, so a code can never collide with a status key. A 3xx only holds. A 400 HTML page is transient under classifier row 4, so it holds and does not count. Departure 3, L-12, F-7, DR-4 (i), DO-1, UD-6 'Why', oauth shape tests, refresh tests 4b, 5 and 7 and the guard row agree. A side effect: a 3xx between two identical answers neither counts nor resets sameError. It is harmless and not reported.

GS-3: resolved. The rollback runs inside replace step 5 under the same lock, and its three branches (admit fails, rewrite succeeds, rewrite fails) match 6.3 step 1, the 4.5 crash row, the store rollback tests (the queued-writer case included), device test 15, DR-2 (e), F-10, U2 pre-mortem 6 and the guard row. I traced a queued refresh of the old account against both rollback outcomes, using the FIFO order of serialized(). The file and live end up agreeing, and the GS-3 store test checks that a reopen and reconcile leaves no orphan.

GS-4: resolved. usable() steps 4-7 send a still-valid token during a hold and throw hold.reason only when a refresh is due and the token has expired. Refresh test 5's 'within 30 s' case uses an expired token, so it stays correct. F-6, DR-4 and T-4 agree. Exception: the dialog text in RF-3.
GS-5: resolved. config.offlineAccess is defaulted from REQUEST_OFFLINE_ACCESS in 6.1 step 4. Device test 2b proves both cases, and T-3, the U5 listing and the guard row name it.

GS-6: resolved. Spec 3.4, 3.9, 6.4 withAccess step 5 and 7.1 agree with the U0 comment and the U5 row: send() originates only CREDENTIAL_ERRORS and passes the request's own rejection and access-token vault errors through. In renew, a local vault failure calls failed(). Refresh test 5 covers it with zero token-endpoint requests and no second decrypt, consistent with usable() step 6.
GS-7: resolved. DO-5 is extended in USER-DECISIONS, in the spec's Day one list and in REQUIREMENTS A-4, and known limit 5 and the DR-4 risk say what happens until the check is done.

GS-8: resolved. The 3.5 fetchLogin comment, 5.1 ('the login read included'), the oauth fetchLogin pins (exact key list; a 302 gives null after one fetch), S-4, T-3, the U1 row and the guard row agree.
GS-9: resolved. Refresh test 6 now reads at 2 s and at 31 s, which tells the 30 s floor from the 1 s floor whether the token is expired or inside the margin. T-4 and the guard row agree.

GS-10: resolved. GitHubAccount.signInId is kept in memory only. replace 'refresh' copies login and signInId from live under the lock, and setLogin(signInId) is used in 6.3 step 3. Device test 17, the store concurrency test, DR-2, the U2 and U5 rows and the traceability row agree. No mention of the old setLogin(accessRef) or from.login is left.

GS-11: resolved. ClearResult is now 'durable'. clear step 4 keeps in retiredRefs any ref whose removal failed. The 8.2 and F-12 texts say 'deleted now, or ... the next time MoonAliza starts'. I checked against src/main/vault.ts: remove unlinks before deleting the index entry, so a failed unlink leaves the entry tombstoned, and the startup reconcile deletes it. The store test's GS-11 case covers this. The F-8 rewording has the gap in RF-1.

Searched all five documents for stale terms: 'removed', rollback(), budget.fresh === 2, from.login, setLogin(accessRef), 'only when the refresh', '5 s' and the clear wording. None is left apart from the findings above.

Departure 7's list of rows changed by GS (F-6..F-8, F-10, F-12, S-4, T-3, T-4, T-9, A-4) matches the (GS-n) markers in REQUIREMENTS.md, and the BREAKDOWN traceability and unit rows name the new tests and seams.
